The main takeaway from our work is that

we identified an isoform switch of a gene in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), which is the most common type of kidney cancer, from the normal isoform (IIIb) to a mesenchymal isoform (IIIc) in 90% of tumors.
the FGFR2 isoforming switch from epithelial to mesenchymal isoform is a common event in ccRCC and is associated with poor patient outcome.

the isoform switch of a single gene (FGFR2), which has a very limited role in the normal kidney, can drive a major portion of the ccRCC transcriptome and methylomes, leading to the misdiagnosis of these tumors as chRCP or ccpRCC.
